title: Building Culture
author: Laura Stam
summary: Stam curates a themed collection of resources on building positive culture in classrooms and schools, framed around the insight that culture is too often left to chance rather than built explicitly and intentionally. The roundup spans podcasts, blog posts, research articles, and videos, covering topics from classroom decor and student buy-in to character development, school-wide habit assemblies, and the hidden curriculum that shapes teacher culture. Featured contributors include Pritesh Raichura (on explicitly teaching values), Joe Kirby (Michaela's 'Bootcamp' approach to instilling mindset and habits), Sara Dower (teaching routines explicitly), and Haili Hughes (on teacher culture). Research anchors from Marzano & Marzano and Kirschner, Hendrick & Heal round out the academic grounding. The collection positions culture-building as an active, teachable discipline—parallel in importance to academic instruction itself.
points: Culture in classrooms and schools profoundly affects success and well-being for students, teachers, and staff—yet it is frequently left to chance rather than built deliberately and explicitly.
Pritesh Raichura's approach explicitly teaches and reinforces values (like integrity) through daily interactions, treating culture-building as parallel in importance to academic instruction.
Joe Kirby's 'Bootcamp' at Michaela teaches pupils the mindset and habits to succeed at school—the 'why' behind every expectation—as a foundation for strong school culture.

Sara Dower's contribution focuses on teaching routines explicitly using systematic, school-grounded examples, while Peps Mccrea's 'Habit Assemblies' provide a whole-school mechanism for establishing a common language around norms.
Haili Hughes reframes the conversation toward teacher culture, examining how school norms shape teachers more than formal policies—a reminder that adult culture matters as much as student culture.
quotes: Culture in the classroom and culture in a school has a huge impact on the success and well-being for students, teachers, and staff. Often I think it is left to chance, but as you will see in the resources below, there are ways to build a positive culture explicitly and intentionally.
This episode is especially pertinent for thinking about how to develop a classroom culture of buy-in as you begin the new year.
More than just classroom set up, Brett shares how the classroom decor (or not to decor) has an impact on classroom culture. This is an excellent read.

Pritesh focuses on explicitly teaching and practicing values to create a strong culture of character in his classroom. This post really shows how teaching culture is just as important as teaching academics.
Joe Kirby writes about Bootcamp at Michaela that includes teaching pupils the mindset and habits to succeed at school and the why behind everything they do.
